rules.whenNoMatch: send the pitch with no sample, then write a note into proposed/
rules.note: Everything ships as draft. Adi flips status to approved after reading. Until then pitches go out with no attachment, which is how her own emails already work.

samples.title: Why Indian Startups Are Betting Big on Your Dog
samples.provenance: Published in The Daily Brief, Zerodha
samples.why: Proof she can take a market nobody has sized properly and make it legible to a general audience, in a real publication.

samples.title: How the LinkedIn Algorithm Actually Works
samples.provenance: Original research across 318,842 posts plus LinkedIn's engineering blog
samples.why: Proof of original quantitative research, not opinion. Useful anywhere distribution is the problem.

samples.title: Delhi's EV mandate is not wrong, it is incomplete
samples.provenance: Her own draft, written from live operating exposure at Bounce
samples.why: Shows she argues from one real person and one real number, not from a position. The strongest single artifact for mobility and gig companies.

samples.title: Naxatra Labs — Density is Destiny
samples.provenance: Brand and content strategy teardown of an axial flux EV motor company
samples.why: Takes a technically correct but soulless B2B company and gives it a narrative, with three audience-specific versions.

samples.title: Three working AI agents, public
samples.why: Running code, not enthusiasm. The right attachment for anyone building with LLMs.

samples.title: Market sizing memo with a defensible capture rate
samples.provenance: Bounce: Rs 49 Cr/month TAM for the next city, 16% capture derived from live operating data
samples.why: The method is hers and it is unusual. Most sizing decks have no defensible capture rate.

samples.title: The unowned-problem memo
samples.provenance: Bounce: eight concurrent workstreams, each from problem statement to live with no team and no budget
samples.why: It is the job, done as the application. Strongest play for founder's office roles.

samples.title: New revenue line, zero to live
samples.provenance: Bounce: rider accessories from nothing, and fleet-as-media advertising
samples.why: She has done this twice, from demand validation to hub-manager training. Few candidates have.

samples.title: Bottleneck map and the AI-assisted rework
samples.provenance: Scaler AI Labs: ~30% manual processing time cut, plus the QA and training systems behind it
samples.why: Names the bottleneck and what the rework returns, rather than promising efficiency.

samples.title: Negotiated-terms sketch
samples.provenance: Bounce: four-insurer evaluation for a 10,000-rider base, negotiated to commercials, commission structure and hub flow
samples.why: Shows she knows what the counterparty wants, not just what she wants.

samples.title: BTL activation plan, on-ground
samples.provenance: Bounce: hub-level accessories sell-through, rider community, rest stops, the company-wide rebrand
samples.why: Below-the-line is where she actually operates. Most marketing candidates only know ATL and paid.
